music_lessons_jam_approach_line: This line aims at a chord tone on beat 1 of all {bars} bars, coming from below in one bar and above in the next.
music_lessons_jam_approach_step_aim: Aim: {note}, a chord tone on beat 1.
music_lessons_jam_approach_text: An approach note is a half step above or below the note you're heading for. Check wants a chord tone on beat 1 of your bars, with the note played just before it a half step away. The score is the share of your bars that do, and the aim is {pct}%, so an empty bar of yours counts as a miss.
music_lessons_jam_approach_title: Lean in from a half step
music_lessons_jam_approach_ways_text: The target is {note}, a tone of {chord}. Tap Next to see each approach.
music_lessons_jam_approach_when_text: The approach note should start in the beat before beat 1, such as on the last beat of the bar before or the and of that beat. It's the last note you play before the target. Either side works, so mix them up.
music_lessons_jam_band_rule: no note may start in the band's bars, apart from a landing in their first half beat and a pickup in their last half beat
music_lessons_jam_bridge_line: This line lands on the 3rd of each bridge change as it arrives, and says nothing in the A sections.
music_lessons_jam_bridge_steps_text: {tune} has a bridge of {chords}. Tap Next to see a 3rd to land on for each.
music_lessons_jam_bridge_text: The A sections aren't scored: rest in them or play the head. In the bridge, land a 3rd or 7th {window} for {pct}% of the changes. A tune with no section marked B is scored on every bar.
music_lessons_jam_charleston_text: The Charleston is one of the best-known rhythms: a note on beat 1 and a note on the and of 2. Here it is in three bars, two over {a} and one over {b}.
music_lessons_jam_displace_beats_text: Here a three-note motif starts on beat 1 of the first bar, on beat 2 of the next and on beat 3 of the one after. So the motif slides later through each bar.
music_lessons_jam_displace_count_text: The aim grows with the form and counts repeats, not bars: {aim} displaced repeats in the {bars} bars of {name}, and {aim12} in a 12-bar form. The sound runs a three-note motif through all {bars} bars, {repeats} displaced repeats, each on the root, 3rd and 5th of the chord where that motif starts.
music_lessons_jam_displace_text: Play a short motif of 2 to 6 notes, then play it again with the same rhythm, starting one beat later in its bar. A repeat counts when it comes no more than two bars after the last one. The pitches are free to change, but leave at least half a beat of silence between motifs.
music_lessons_jam_displace_title: The same idea, a beat later
music_lessons_jam_fills_bar_text: The head here plays two notes, then rests for two beats. Tap Next to fill the rest.
music_lessons_jam_fills_line: This plays the head's notes in all {bars} bars with a two-note fill in each rest.
music_lessons_jam_fills_step_fill: A fill of two notes, {a} and {b}, inside the rest.
music_lessons_jam_fills_step_head: The head: {a} and {b}, then two beats of rest.
music_lessons_jam_fills_text: Play the head, and fill its rests of two beats or more. Check wants {pct}% of the head's notes played, in any octave and within half a beat of where the head puts them. A fill is 2 to 4 notes that start inside the rest but not in its last half beat, and the aim is {fills} filled rests a chorus, or all of them if the head has fewer.
music_lessons_jam_guide_check_text: At least {set}% of your notes must be a guide tone of the chord sounding, or of the one arriving within half a beat. A guide tone must also land {window} for {landings}% of the changes. On a 6th chord the 6th stands in for the 7th.
music_lessons_jam_guide_line_text: Each chord's first bar has its two guide tones, one on beat 1 and one on beat 3, then the second bar rests. The pairs are {pairs}, for {chords}.
music_lessons_jam_guide_name_text: The 3rd says whether a chord is major or minor, and the 7th says what kind of seventh it is. Together they're the guide tones. In {chord} they are {a} and {b}.
music_lessons_jam_guide_name_title: The notes that name a chord
music_lessons_jam_guide_through_text: Tap Next to follow the guide tones through {a}, {b} and {c}. Each one moves by no more than a half step.
music_lessons_jam_intro_blues_scale: Use only the key's blues scale: the 1, b3, 4, b5, 5 and b7.
music_lessons_jam_intro_pentatonic_1: Use only the minor pentatonic on the key's tonic: its 1, b3, 4, 5 and b7.
music_lessons_jam_intro_pentatonic_2: Use only the minor pentatonic a step above the key's tonic: its 1, b3, 4, 5 and b7.
music_lessons_jam_intro_pentatonic_5: Use only the minor pentatonic a fifth above the key's tonic: its 1, b3, 4, 5 and b7.
music_lessons_jam_intro_three_notes: Use only the key's 1, b3 and 5, the notes of a minor triad.
music_lessons_jam_motif_line: That plays the Charleston in all {bars} bars of {chords}, so every bar has the same rhythm and a chord tone on beat 1.
music_lessons_jam_motif_new_text: Tap Next to see the same rhythm take a chord tone from each chord. Beat 1 gets the root and the and of 2 gets the 3rd.
music_lessons_jam_motif_step: {chord}: {a} on beat 1, {b} on the and of 2.
music_lessons_jam_motif_text: Pick the rhythm of one bar and repeat it as the chords change. Check compares where your notes start, to the nearest eighth note, so only the start times matter. Use the same rhythm in at least {motif}% of your bars, with a chord tone on beat 1 in {downbeats}% of them.
music_lessons_jam_move_down_half: {from} moves down a half step to {to}, now the {role}
music_lessons_jam_move_down_whole: {from} moves down a whole step to {to}, now the {role}
music_lessons_jam_move_up_half: {from} moves up a half step to {to}, now the {role}
music_lessons_jam_move_up_whole: {from} moves up a whole step to {to}, now the {role}
music_lessons_jam_offbeat_line: This line starts a short phrase on the and of 1 in every bar, then stops for the rest of the bar.
music_lessons_jam_offbeat_text: A phrase is a run of notes with less than a beat of silence between them, so a pause of a beat or more starts a new one. Each new phrase should begin clearly between beats, such as on the and of 1 or the and of 4. The score is the share that do, and the aim is {pct}%.
music_lessons_jam_quote_example_text: Say the head opens with these four notes. Hear them, then the same four an octave lower, which is a quote. After that, develop it in your own way.
music_lessons_jam_quote_text: Open each A section with a run of at least four notes from the head: the same pitch names and the same steps between them, in any octave. A repeated note counts once. The run must start from half a beat before the section up to two bars into it, and the aim is {pct}% of the A sections.
music_lessons_jam_set_blue_text: Here the {note} is the blue third: over a C or C7 chord it rubs against the chord's E on purpose. {check}
music_lessons_jam_set_check: Check scores the share of your notes in the set, and the aim is {pct}%, in any octave.
music_lessons_jam_set_line_text: This plays the {count} notes up and back down. Only the notes are scored in this game, not time or rests.
music_lessons_jam_set_rests_text: Rests count too: the aim is {count} silences of two beats or more in a chorus, measured from when you let go of a note. This line plays two notes, then rests for two beats, in every bar.
music_lessons_jam_set_text: {intro} These numbers count up the key's scale from its tonic (b means a half step lower), so in the key of C that's {names}. On the stage, the ringed keys are numbered from the current chord's root instead.
music_lessons_jam_slip_land_text: This line slips the first four notes of each chord's scale up a half step, then plays a chord tone on the next beat. The slip is the tension and the chord tone is the release.
music_lessons_jam_slip_step_plain: The first four notes of the {chord} scale: {notes}.
music_lessons_jam_slip_step_slipped: A half step higher: {notes}. {count} of the 4 are outside {chord} and its scale.
music_lessons_jam_slip_text: A side-slip is a phrase of three or more notes that are neither chord tones nor in the chord's scale, played within a beat of each other with no two inside notes in a row. It ends by resolving to a chord tone on the next beat, no more than a beat and a half after the last slip note. The aim is {slips} slips a chorus, with {pct}% of them resolved.
music_lessons_jam_slip_up_text: One way in: take a phrase from the scale and play it all a half step higher. Tap Next to try it on {chord}.
music_lessons_jam_thirds_line: The line lands on {notes} as the changes arrive, holding each for two beats. When the form comes back round to a different chord, that counts as a change too.
music_lessons_jam_thirds_text: Land on the 3rd of every chord that differs from the one before, {window}. The score is the share of changes landed, and the aim is {aim}%. A 7th doesn't count here, and on a sus chord the 4th stands in for the 3rd.
music_lessons_jam_tones_line_changes: {chord} has {tones}. The line puts the 3rd on each change, then the 5th, 7th and root in turn, all on beats 1 and 3.
music_lessons_jam_tones_line_tones: {chord} has {tones}. The line plays the 3rd, 5th, 7th and root of each chord in turn, all on beats 1 and 3.
music_lessons_jam_tones_text_changes: A note that starts on beat 1 or 3 (within a quarter of a beat) should be a tone of the chord sounding, for {strong}% of them. A 3rd or 7th (lit here on {chord}) should land {window} for {landings}% of the changes. Your weakest of the two sets the score, and in a waltz only beat 1 counts.
music_lessons_jam_tones_text_tones: Every note that starts on beat 1 or 3 (within a quarter of a beat) must be a tone of the chord sounding (lit here on {chord}). The score is the share that are, and the aim is {strong}%. Notes on the other beats are free, and in a waltz only beat 1 counts.
music_lessons_jam_window: from half a beat before a change to a beat after it
music_lessons_jam_windows_line_call: The picture shows only your answers: nothing in the band's bars, then two notes in each of yours. The sound plays your answers too, and the band plays the calls in the drill.
music_lessons_jam_windows_line_space: The picture and the sound show your part: two notes in each of your bars and nothing in the band's.
music_lessons_jam_windows_text_call: The band plays a call for {band}, then you answer for {you}. A note must start in your answer, but {rule}. The score is the share of stretches kept, yours and the band's, and the aim is {pct}%.
music_lessons_jam_windows_text_space: You play for {you}, then the band has {band} to itself, all chorus. A note must start in each of your stretches, but {rule}. The score is the share of stretches kept, yours and the band's, and the aim is {pct}%.
music_lessons_pads_breaks_text: A break is a short drum part lifted from a record, written out for you to play. The {groove} runs for {bars} bars and the bars differ, so keep count of where you are. The grid shows its kick and snare in bars 1 and 4.
music_lessons_pads_builds_text: The build goes {runs}, louder all the way. It's scored on how steadily the level climbs and on covering at least {span} percent of your soft to loud range. That needs pads that send velocity.
music_lessons_pads_chop_edit_plays_gap: It plays {step} a step: slices {slices} (a gap lets the slice before it ring).
music_lessons_pads_chop_edit_source: It is written for the {loop} loop.
music_lessons_pads_chop_free_extra: It needs at least {hits} hits, and passes at {repeat} percent of them played again and {time} percent on time.
music_lessons_pads_chop_len_text: A one-bar loop gives slices of {one}, a two-bar loop {two} and a four-bar loop {four}. Played in order, slices 1 to {count} bring the loop back.
music_lessons_pads_chop_loop_text: A chop cuts a loop into {count} equal slices, one on each pad from {first} to {last}. Hear it plays the {loop} loop whole, and Next lights slices 1 to 4 in turn.
music_lessons_pads_chop_reorder_extra: The Order choice picks the edit.
music_lessons_pads_chop_up_text: Chopping plays the slices in a new order: the {edit} edit plays slices {slices}. Slices {never} never play.
music_lessons_pads_count16_text: Count each beat in four: 1 e & a. The {phrase} plays on {counts}. Tap Hear it and count along.
music_lessons_pads_dance_floor_text: House and disco put the kick on every beat, called four on the floor. The open hat plays on every &, between the kicks. The lit pads are the ones "{groove}" uses.
music_lessons_pads_dance_half_text: Trap feels half as fast as its tempo, with the clap only on {clap}. Drum and bass plays its kick on {kick}, at up to {bpm} BPM. Tap each to hear a bar at its starting tempo.
music_lessons_pads_dilla_text: Two feels at once: the hats swing at {swing} while the snare comes about {ms} ms early at {bpm} BPM, a little more at slower tempos. The drill times your snare against that early spot. Tap Pushed, then On the beat, to hear the difference.
music_lessons_pads_dyn_crescendo_text: A bar of sixteenths from as soft as you can to your loudest. It passes when the levels climb steadily (a rank correlation of {rho} or more), cover at least {span} percent of your range, and no hit is missed. Hear it on a typical range.
music_lessons_pads_dyn_even_text: Sixteen hits at the same level. It passes when they vary by less than {spread} percent of your range, measured as the spread, and no hit is missed. Hear it on a typical range.
music_lessons_pads_dyn_ladder_text: Sixteen hits in four groups of four, each group in the next quarter of your range, softest first. The run is correct with at least {pass} percent of hits in their quarter. Hear it on a typical range.
music_lessons_pads_echo_answer: Your answer is the same bar, played in the bar after the call.
music_lessons_pads_echo_call: The call is one bar: kick on {kick}, snare on {snare}.
music_lessons_pads_echo_level_ghosts: Some calls have ghost notes, played at the ghost level.
music_lessons_pads_echo_level_grid: The grid shows the first call.
music_lessons_pads_echo_listen_text: The app plays a bar, then the next bar is yours: play back what you heard. There are four rounds, each a call and an answer, and only your answers are scored. The grid stays hidden until the run is over.
music_lessons_pads_echo_pass_text: A round counts as played back when at least {pass} percent of its notes are matched. The run is correct when all four rounds are played back and you play no extra hits. Playing along with a call costs nothing, because only the answer bars are scored.
music_lessons_pads_echo_round_text: Tap Next to hear a call and then the answer that matches it.
music_lessons_pads_echo_together: Together: the call, then your answer.
music_lessons_pads_fill_card_rock: It comes after three bars of rock. The lit pads are the ones the fill bar and the landing use. The drill times the {count} notes it adds to the groove for rushing.
music_lessons_pads_fill_card_shuffle: It comes after three bars of shuffle. The lit pads are the ones the fill bar and the landing use. The drill times the {count} notes it adds to the groove for rushing.
music_lessons_pads_fills_groove_text: A fill is a short burst of drum hits that marks the end of a phrase. In these grooves it's the last bar of four, and the next phrase starts back on the one. The grid shows the last two bars of "{groove}".
music_lessons_pads_fills_land_text: The landing counts when crash and kick are both within {ms} ms of the click on the one. Tap Landed to hear them there, or Late to hear both {demo} ms behind.
music_lessons_pads_fills_run_text: A run is three bars of groove, a fill in bar 4, then crash and kick together on the next one. The grid shows one groove bar and the fill bar, and Hear it plays them with the landing.
music_lessons_pads_fills_rush_text: If the fill's notes come more than {ms} ms early on average, the fill counts as rushed and the run isn't clean. Tap On time, or Rushed to hear the fill {demo} ms early.
music_lessons_pads_hear_play_text: Hear it first plays the phrase before you try it. Each phrase starts slow, and clean runs raise the tempo toward its goal. At the goal, Move on offers the next phrase.
music_lessons_pads_hold_text: Note Repeat plays a pad again for as long as you hold it, on a grid set by the rate. The app changes the rate as the chart goes, so you hold the pad and follow the chart. The drill names the pad to hold.
music_lessons_pads_independence_text: In an independence groove each hand or foot plays a part of its own and holds it whatever the others do. In "{groove}" the hats play the same in every bar while the kick takes a new pattern each bar. The grid shows its first two bars.
music_lessons_pads_latin_332_text: Count each beat in four sixteenths: 1 e & a. The tresillo puts three notes in eight sixteenths, spaced 3 + 3 + 2, on {first}. Then it starts again on {again}.
music_lessons_pads_latin_groove_text: Many Caribbean and Latin grooves are built on it. In "{groove}" the kick plays the first two notes and the snare the third, while {styles} play the last two on the snare over a kick on every beat. Hear one bar of {grooveLower}.
music_lessons_pads_levels_text: Each section has a level against your own soft to loud range: soft is {softLow} to {softHigh} percent of it, medium {mediumLow} to {mediumHigh} and loud {loudLow} to {loudHigh}. In written music these are p, mf and f, and a rising section is a crescendo. Tap each to hear eight snare hits on a typical range.
music_lessons_pads_linear_text: In a linear groove no two drums play at the same time, so the hands and the foot take turns. In "{groove}" the hats, snare and kick pass the bar round without overlapping. The grid shows its bar.
music_lessons_pads_meter_text: Odd-meter grooves have 5 or 7 counts in a bar instead of 4. Count them in groups of two and three, for example 5 as 3 + 2. In 7/8 each count is an eighth note.
music_lessons_pads_names_text: A phrase is a short rhythm drummers know by name: clave cells, a tag ending, a fill and its landing, a build. They run {min} to {max} bars, and the setup lists them easiest first.
music_lessons_pads_orch_card_text: {detail}. The drill plays two bars of sixteenth paradiddles with the first stroke of each group of four accented, and the example plays one.
music_lessons_pads_orch_card_text_no_kic: {detail}. The drill plays two bars of sixteenth paradiddles with the first stroke of each group of four accented, and the example plays one. This one has no kick.
music_lessons_pads_orch_hear_text: Tap Next to hear each group of four, then the whole bar.
music_lessons_pads_orch_sticking_text: The paradiddle is {paradiddle}, two groups of four. In this drill each hand gets its own drum, so the sticking becomes a groove: two bars of sixteenths with the first stroke of each group accented.
music_lessons_pads_orch_which_text: {detail}, as the {choice} choice plays it. The lit pads show each hand, and K is the kick.
music_lessons_pads_orch_whole: Four groups make one bar of sixteenths, the paradiddle twice through.
music_lessons_pads_ost_clave_text: The rim plays the son clave on {counts}. The kick plays a different pattern in each of the four bars under it. The grid shows the clave.
music_lessons_pads_ost_hats_text: Tap Next to hear the hi-hat alone and then with a snare line on top.
music_lessons_pads_ost_keep_text: An ostinato is a part that repeats without changing while another part moves. The {hats} keep eighths while the snare reads a line, or the kick when you choose that for new lines, and for the clave line the {clave} keeps the son clave. You play two bars of the ostinato alone, then four bars with the line.
music_lessons_pads_ost_line_step: Then the snare reads a line on {counts} while the hats carry on.
music_lessons_pads_ost_line_text: The snare plays on {counts}. The hats play eighths under it.
music_lessons_pads_ost_read_text: Four new bars to read come up on every run, built from short patterns, with at least three notes a bar and never plain quarters. You choose who reads, {readers}. The grid shows one example bar read on the snare.
music_lessons_pads_ost_scored_text: The drill counts how many ostinato notes you hit alone, then under the line. The ostinato holds when the rate under the line is no more than {drop} percentage points below the rate alone. The run also needs the groove itself to be correct.
music_lessons_pads_phrase_bars: {feel} It runs {bars} bars. Hear it at {bpm} BPM, its starting tempo.
music_lessons_pads_phrase_one_pad: {feel} It's all on the {name} pad, on {counts}.
music_lessons_pads_phrase_steps: {feel} Tap Next to add a pad.
music_lessons_pads_pressure_text: If your pads send aftertouch, pressure sets the level of the repeats. If they don't, every repeat keeps the level of your first hit.
music_lessons_pads_range_text: Every controller and every hand differ, so the drill first asks for your own range. Calibrate takes four of your softest hits, then four of your loudest, and keeps the average of each. Every level is then read as a share of the space between them.
music_lessons_pads_rate_text: At {rate} a held pad repeats {count} times a beat, which is {sub}. Hear two beats of it. Each repeat keeps your hit's level unless your pads send aftertouch.
music_lessons_pads_rolls_text: A roll plays notes faster than sixteenths: thirty-seconds, {per32} to a beat, or sixteenth triplets, {per16t} to a beat. Alternate two fingers on one pad, or hold Note Repeat at 1/32 or 1/16T. Hear the hats of "{groove}".
music_lessons_pads_rud_accent_many: The accents are strokes {strokes} of each {count}.
music_lessons_pads_rud_accent_one: The accent is stroke {stroke} of each {count}.
music_lessons_pads_rud_accents_text: With pads that send changing velocity, each accent should land at {accentLow} to {accentHigh} percent of full level and each tap at {tapLow} to {tapHigh} percent. Tap Even, then Accent and taps, to hear four sixteenths each way.
music_lessons_pads_rud_any_sub: It uses the subdivision you pick.
music_lessons_pads_rud_doubles_step: Double strokes play each hand twice: {sticking}.
music_lessons_pads_rud_flam: Each stroke has a grace note on the other pad {ms} ms before it, and only the main strokes are scored.
music_lessons_pads_rud_kinds_text: Tap Next to reveal each one, then Hear this step. L is the left hand and R the right.
music_lessons_pads_rud_moving: The accent moves one note later each beat.
music_lessons_pads_rud_one_pad: Two fingers on one pad, {sticking}, repeated.
music_lessons_pads_rud_para_step: The paradiddle is {paradiddle}, the sticking the Rudiments on the kit drill uses. This drill starts it on the left hand, {sticking}, the same pattern with the other hand first.
music_lessons_pads_rud_per_beat: It plays {counts} notes in successive beats, timed on its closest spacing, {sub}.
music_lessons_pads_rud_sub_text: The subdivision is how many strokes fit in a beat: two for eighths, three for triplets, four for sixteenths. Tap each to hear four beats of single strokes, and watch the grid.
music_lessons_pads_rud_two_hands_text: A rudiment is a sticking: which hand plays each stroke, left (L) on {left} and right (R) on {right}. Tap Next to play this drill's paradiddle, {sticking}, one stroke at a time.
music_lessons_pads_section_pass_text: A section passes with at least {matched} percent of its notes matched and no more than {extra} percent of them as extra hits (one is always allowed). When your pads send velocity, its level must be in band too. The run is correct when every section passes.
music_lessons_pads_shuffle_text: In a shuffle each beat splits into three, counted 1 trip let, and many shuffles skip the middle note. The grid for these grooves has three steps a beat, or six in the grooves that go finer. The picture shows the hi-hat of "{groove}".
music_lessons_pads_six_bar_text: Here is "{groove}", one bar at a time. Tap Next to add a part.
music_lessons_pads_six_count_text: From level 3 many grooves put notes between the eighths. Count each beat 1 e & a, four sixteenths to a beat. The grid marks hi-hat hits on every sixteenth of one bar.
music_lessons_pads_six_ghost_text: A ghost note is a very quiet hit, here on the snare between the backbeats. On the 0 to 127 scale the drill's bands are {ghostLow} to {ghostHigh} for a ghost, {normalLow} to {normalHigh} for a normal hit and {accentLow} and up for an accent. It checks them only when your pads send changing velocity.
music_lessons_pads_six_ghosts: The soft ghost snares sit on {counts}.
music_lessons_pads_six_swing_text: Swing delays every second sixteenth. The drill gives it as a percentage of the eighth, from 50 for straight up to 75, where 66 sits on the triplet, and offers it on grooves that can swing. Tap Straight or Swung to hear sixteenth hats at 50 and at {swung}.
music_lessons_pads_song_card_text: The sections are {sections}. It starts at {start} BPM and aims for {target}.
music_lessons_pads_stick_text: Page one of Stick Control is every four-note sticking of R and L, {count} in all, in eighths. You play each {times} times on one pad a hand, so the app can check the sticking. The label gives the sticking, such as {sticking}.
music_lessons_pads_swing_feel_text: Count the beats, not the late notes: the swung one should feel lazy, not placed. On a swung groove the results show Swing played, where your notes on the e and the a landed against the groove's swing. It doesn't change the pass.
music_lessons_pads_swing_late_text: Swing delays every second sixteenth, the e and the a, while notes on the beat and the & stay put. The Swing choice runs from {min}, straight, to {max}, and 66 sits on the triplet. Tap each to hear sixteenth hats.
music_lessons_pads_take_text: A piece is a list of sections, such as an intro, a groove, a build and a drop. You play it from start to end in one take, and each section is scored on its own.
music_lessons_pads_three_text: The setup offers four levels, a crescendo, and even hits, each {counts} hits long. After a run the results draw each hit's level in your range against where it should be.
music_lessons_pads_velocity_text: How hard you strike a pad is its velocity, a MIDI number from 1 to 127. The drill reads it from the MPC with Full Level off, and the pads on screen send none. Tap Soft and Loud to hear the two ends.
music_lessons_reading_acc_flat_text: A flat sign lowers a note by a half step, the next key down. Here {note} is followed by {next}, in F major.
music_lessons_reading_acc_natural_text: In F major every B is played as {flat}, so the first B has no sign. A natural sign cancels that flat for the note it sits beside, and the second note is a plain {plain}.
music_lessons_reading_acc_sharp_text: A sharp sign raises a note by a half step, the next key up on the piano. Here {note} is followed by {next}, in C major.
music_lessons_reading_boc_boosts_text: Tap Flat, then each band boosted by {db} dB, and notice that the sound gains something.
music_lessons_reading_boc_cuts_text: Now each band cut by {db} dB. The sound loses something, and each cut sounds different from the boost at the same band.
music_lessons_reading_boc_gain_text: Here every change is {db} dB. Tap Flat, then the 1 kHz band boosted and cut by that much.
music_lessons_reading_boc_intro_text: Changed has one band either boosted or cut. You decide which, and the band doesn't matter for the answer. Changed is turned up or down to match Flat's loudness, so a louder sound isn't the clue.
music_lessons_reading_cell_dotted_eighth: A dotted eighth note lasts three sixteenths, so the note after it falls on the a of the same beat. In this bar notes start on {names}.
music_lessons_reading_cell_dotted_quarte: A dotted quarter note lasts one and a half beats, so the next note falls on an &. In this bar notes start on {names}.
music_lessons_reading_cell_rests_text_co: A rest is a silent beat, and a dotted half note is held through both beats of the bar. In this bar one note starts on {names} and is held to the end.
music_lessons_reading_cell_rests_text_si: A rest is a silent beat, and a half note is held through two beats. In this bar a note starts on {names}.
music_lessons_reading_cell_swing_text: Swung eighths are played long and short, about two to one, but counted and written as straight eighths 1 &. The second note of each pair comes late.
music_lessons_reading_cell_syncopation_t: Syncopation puts a note on an & and holds it over the next number, so that number has no note starting on it. In this bar notes start on {names}.
music_lessons_reading_cell_triplets_text: A triplet fits three even notes into one beat. They fall between the counts of the e, & and a grid, so tap them evenly across the beat.
music_lessons_reading_changing_text: The time signature changes every 2 bars, through {list} in turn.
music_lessons_reading_check_meter: Check the time signature before you start, and at every bar where it changes.
music_lessons_reading_comp_hear_text: Tap Flat, then {light} and {heavy}. The levels are matched, so each is as loud as Flat overall.
music_lessons_reading_comp_intro_text: A compressor turns down the loudest parts so the sound is more even. Changed is Flat with light compression, heavy compression, or none, and you name which.
music_lessons_reading_comp_tip: Listen to the hits. Heavy compression flattens them more than light compression does, so the loop sounds smaller and more even.
music_lessons_reading_count_compound_ex: A note on a number starts on the beat, and the & and the a are the two places after it.
music_lessons_reading_count_compound_tex: In 6/8 the beat is a dotted quarter, so a bar has two beats. Each beat splits in three, so a bar is counted {counts}.
music_lessons_reading_count_eighths_ex: A note on a number starts on the beat, and a note on an & starts in the second half of it.
music_lessons_reading_count_eighths_text: Count 1 2 3 4 with the click, one number on each click. Between two numbers sits an &, the second half of the beat, so a bar is counted {counts}.
music_lessons_reading_count_sixteenths_e: Each beat has four places to put a note, and the number comes first.
music_lessons_reading_count_sixteenths_t: Sixteenth notes split each beat in four, counted with e, & and a after the number. A bar is counted {counts}.
music_lessons_reading_delay_card_text: Tap Flat, then an echo of {delay}, and listen for how long after a hit the repeat lands.
music_lessons_reading_delay_text: Changed has an echo, a repeat of the sound a short time later. The loop runs at {bpm} BPM, so the times are note values.
music_lessons_reading_delay_tip: The longer the delay, the further the echo lands from the hit. Listen for where the repeat falls against the beat.
music_lessons_reading_echo_listen: Listen and count: the bar plays once.
music_lessons_reading_echo_text: One bar plays over the click, then you tap the same rhythm on the next bar. Tap Next to see it.
music_lessons_reading_echo_title: Hear it, then tap it back
music_lessons_reading_echo_your_turn: Your turn: tap on {names}. Each tap lands on its count.
music_lessons_reading_eq_band_text_boost: Tap Flat, then {band} boosted by {db} dB. Listen for {what}.
music_lessons_reading_eq_band_text_cut: Tap Flat, then {band} cut by {db} dB. Listen for {what}.
music_lessons_reading_eq_cut_text: Each question gives you one loop in two versions. Flat is untouched, and Changed has one band cut, like the dip drawn here. Flip between them as often as you like, then name the band.
music_lessons_reading_eq_cut_tip: Cutting a low band makes the sound thinner, and cutting a high band makes it duller. Go back to Flat often, because you're listening for what's gone.
music_lessons_reading_eq_gain_text_boost: Here every band is boosted by {db} dB, about one octave wide. Tap Flat, then the 1 kHz band at that size.
music_lessons_reading_eq_gain_text_cut: Here every band is cut by {db} dB, about one octave wide. Tap Flat, then the 1 kHz band at that size.
music_lessons_reading_eq_peak_text: Each question gives you one loop in two versions. Flat is untouched, and Changed has one band boosted, like the bump drawn here. Flip between them as often as you like, then name the band.
music_lessons_reading_eq_peak_tip: Boosting a low band makes the sound heavier or boomier, and boosting a high band makes it brighter or hissier. A band you miss comes back more often.
music_lessons_reading_grid_count_text: Each column is one count, with the number on the beat and {subs} after it. You mark a cell where a note starts.
music_lessons_reading_grid_ear_text: Say the count as the rhythm plays, and mark the cell for every note you hear. These notes fall on {names}.
music_lessons_reading_grid_ear_title: From the ear to the grid
music_lessons_reading_grid_rests_text: Mark only where a note starts. A rest, or the rest of a held note, leaves its cells empty.
music_lessons_reading_grid_title: Writing a rhythm on the grid
music_lessons_reading_item_chords_lh_tex: On some strong beats the left hand plays the melody note with one or two lower notes. Play them together.
music_lessons_reading_item_chords_rh_tex: On some strong beats the right hand plays the melody note with one or two lower notes. Play them together.
music_lessons_reading_item_clef_change_t: For a bar or two the left hand may read in the treble clef. A small clef sign on the staff marks the change, and a bass clef sign marks the return.
music_lessons_reading_item_dotted_eighth: A dotted eighth note is an eighth note plus a sixteenth note. A dotted eighth and a sixteenth together are as long as a quarter note.
music_lessons_reading_item_dotted_quarte: A dotted quarter note is a quarter note plus an eighth note, so it's as long as three eighth notes. A dot always adds half of the note's own length.
music_lessons_reading_item_pickup_text: Some phrases open with a pickup: the first bar opens with rests, and only its last note is played. Count the rests silently and come in on that note.
music_lessons_reading_item_sixteenths_te: Four sixteenth notes make one quarter note, and two make an eighth note. Sixteenths are written with two beams or two flags.
music_lessons_reading_item_swing_text: Swing eighths are written straight but played long and short, about two to one. Lean on the first of each pair.
music_lessons_reading_item_syncopation_t: In syncopation a long note starts halfway between two quarter-note pulses and is held across the next pulse. Nothing new starts in that line on that pulse, so keep counting through the held note.
music_lessons_reading_item_ties_text: A tie is a curved line joining two notes of the same pitch. Play the first, hold through the second, and don't play it again.
music_lessons_reading_item_triplets_text: A triplet puts three even notes in the time of two of the same kind. Three eighth note triplets take the time of one quarter note.
music_lessons_reading_ks_add_many_flat: Tap Next to add the {count} flats one at a time, in the order they are written.
music_lessons_reading_ks_add_many_sharp: Tap Next to add the {count} sharps one at a time, in the order they are written.
music_lessons_reading_ks_add_one_flat: Tap Next to add the flat.
music_lessons_reading_ks_add_one_sharp: Tap Next to add the sharp.
music_lessons_reading_ks_intro_text: The sharps or flats right after the clef are the key signature. They hold for every bar, so no sign is written beside each note.
music_lessons_reading_ks_intro_title: Signs at the start of the staff
music_lessons_reading_ks_note_flat: With this key signature the note shown is {letter} flat, though no sign is written beside it. Every {letter} in the piece is played the same way, unless a sign beside a note says otherwise.
music_lessons_reading_ks_note_sharp: With this key signature the note shown is {letter} sharp, though no sign is written beside it. Every {letter} in the piece is played the same way, unless a sign beside a note says otherwise.
music_lessons_reading_ks_step_flat: {letter} flat: every {letter}, in every octave, is played a half step lower.
music_lessons_reading_ks_step_sharp: {letter} sharp: every {letter}, in every octave, is played a half step higher.
music_lessons_reading_level_card_text: Tap Flat, then a step of {db} dB, and notice the size of the jump.
music_lessons_reading_level_text: Changed is Flat made louder by a few dB. You name how much.
music_lessons_reading_level_tip: The smaller the step, the harder it is to tell from Flat. Flip back and forth quickly, because a level is easier to compare in a moment than from memory.
music_lessons_reading_listen_text: Count the beats out loud while the rhythm plays over the click. Notice which counts get a note, and which stay silent.
music_lessons_reading_ls_landmark_text_b: The two dots of the bass clef sit either side of the fourth line, so that line is {note}. Count up or down from it to find any other note.
music_lessons_reading_ls_landmark_text_t: The treble clef curls around the second line, so that line is {note}. Count up or down from it to find any other note.
music_lessons_reading_ls_ledger_text_bas: A note too high or too low for the five lines sits on short extra lines called ledger lines. Middle C is on the first ledger line above the bass staff, and {note} is on the first one below. The figure shows two notes on ledger lines on each side.
music_lessons_reading_ls_ledger_text_tre: A note too high or too low for the five lines sits on short extra lines called ledger lines. Middle C is on the first ledger line below the treble staff, and {note} is on the first one above. The figure shows two notes on ledger lines on each side.
music_lessons_reading_ls_lines_text_bass: A staff has five lines, counted from the bottom. In the bass clef they are {letters}. Good Boys Do Fine Always gives you the order.
music_lessons_reading_ls_lines_text_treb: A staff has five lines, counted from the bottom. In the treble clef they are {letters}. Every Good Boy Does Fine gives you the order.
music_lessons_reading_ls_spaces_text_bas: The four spaces between the lines, from the bottom, are {letters} in the bass clef. All Cows Eat Grass.
music_lessons_reading_ls_spaces_text_tre: The four spaces between the lines, from the bottom, are {letters} in the treble clef. They spell the word FACE.
music_lessons_reading_meter_2_2: 2/2 has two half-note beats in a bar, so a half note is one beat and a quarter note is half a beat.
music_lessons_reading_meter_3_8: 3/8 has three eighth notes in a bar, counted 1 2 3.
music_lessons_reading_meter_5_4: 5/4 has five quarter notes in a bar, grouped as three and two or as two and three.
music_lessons_reading_meter_5_8: 5/8 has five eighth notes in a bar, grouped as two and three or as three and two.
music_lessons_reading_meter_7_8: 7/8 has seven eighth notes in a bar, grouped in twos and threes.
music_lessons_reading_meter_9_8: 9/8 has nine eighth notes in a bar, in three beats of three, counted 1 & a 2 & a 3 & a.
music_lessons_reading_meter_compound: In 6/8 the beat is a dotted quarter, so a bar has two beats of three eighth notes, counted 1 & a 2 & a.
music_lessons_reading_notes_fall_on: In this bar the notes fall on {names}.
music_lessons_reading_pan_card_text: Tap Flat, then {pos}, and notice where the sound sits.
music_lessons_reading_pan_text: Changed is Flat moved to one place between the left and the right speaker. Centre is an answer too, and then Changed sounds in the same place as Flat.
music_lessons_reading_pan_tip: Headphones or two speakers both work, but headphones make the position clearest. Left means the sound sits more in your left ear.
music_lessons_reading_rest_dotted_eighth: A dotted eighth rest is silent as long as a dotted eighth note, three sixteenth notes.
music_lessons_reading_rest_dotted_half: A dotted half rest is silent as long as a dotted half note, three quarter notes.
music_lessons_reading_rest_dotted_quarte: A dotted quarter rest is silent as long as a dotted quarter note, three eighth notes.
music_lessons_reading_rest_dotted_sixtee: A dotted sixteenth rest is silent as long as a dotted sixteenth note, three thirty-second notes.
music_lessons_reading_rest_eighth: An eighth rest is silent as long as an eighth note, two sixteenth notes.
music_lessons_reading_rest_half: A half rest is silent as long as a half note, two quarter notes.
music_lessons_reading_rest_quarter: A quarter rest is silent as long as a quarter note, two eighth notes.
music_lessons_reading_rest_sixteenth: A sixteenth rest is silent as long as a sixteenth note, two thirty-second notes.
music_lessons_reading_rest_thirty_second: A thirty-second rest is silent as long as a thirty-second note, half a sixteenth note.
music_lessons_reading_rest_whole: A whole rest is silent as long as a whole note, four quarter notes.
music_lessons_reading_rests_long_text: A rest is a silence as long as the note it's named after. The whole rest hangs below a line and the half rest sits on top of one. Tap Next to see each rest after its note.
music_lessons_reading_rests_shorter_text: A dot after a rest adds half its length, as it does after a note. Tap Next to see each one.
music_lessons_reading_rests_shortest_tex: More flags make a shorter rest. Tap Next to see each one.
music_lessons_reading_satb_text: Four notes are stacked across the grand staff, and the lowest is the root of the chord. The root is doubled above it. Name the triad by its three notes from the root up, like C-E-G, with the doubled note once.
music_lessons_reading_triad_text: A triad is three notes stacked in thirds, so they sit on three lines in a row or three spaces in a row. Name it by its three notes from the bottom, like C-E-G.
music_lessons_reading_val_eighth: An eighth note lasts half a beat, so eight fill the bar. Counted 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &, two fit in each beat.
music_lessons_reading_val_half: A half note lasts 2 beats, so two fill the bar.
music_lessons_reading_val_quarter: A quarter note lasts 1 beat, so four fill the bar.
music_lessons_reading_val_whole: A whole note lasts 4 beats, so one fills the bar.
music_lessons_reading_values_dots_text: A dot adds half the note's length. In this bar the dotted half note lasts 3 beats, and the quarter rest is the last beat of silence.
music_lessons_reading_values_length_text: In 4/4 a bar has 4 beats, counted 1 2 3 4. Tap Next to see how long each note value lasts.
music_lessons_reading_values_time_sig_te: The top number of a time signature says how many notes of one length fit in a bar, and the bottom number names that length. 4/4 holds four quarter notes, 3/4 three, and 6/8 six eighth notes. This bar is 3/4, counted 1 2 3.
music_lessons_technique_art_beat_text: The drill plays a click at the top bar's tempo. You tongue the same note once on each click, for as many notes as you set.
music_lessons_technique_art_checks_text: It checks that every note is the target, how long each sounds against the style, and how close each attack lands to its click. An attack counts within {window} ms, or a quarter of the beat if that's less. Note length needs the Aerophone's own note-offs, so the on-screen chart can't measure it.
music_lessons_technique_art_sensor_text: A tongued note stops the air for a moment, so the breath dips. The drill counts a dip under {dip} percent of your usual breath as a tongue stop, and the rise after it as the attack. It reads the breath because the instrument may keep sounding and send no new note.
music_lessons_technique_art_styles_text: Staccato lets each note sound about {staccato} percent of the beat, and legato about {legato} percent. Tap each style to hear it at 100 beats a minute.
music_lessons_technique_bend_checks_text: A whole step is 200 cents and a half step 100. In tune is within {inTune} cents of the target and close is within {close}. Past that it says flat, so push further, or sharp, so ease off.
music_lessons_technique_bend_frets_text: A bend pushes a fretted string across the neck to raise its pitch. A half step bend reaches the note 1 fret higher on the same string, and a whole step bend the note 2 frets higher.
music_lessons_technique_bend_frets_title: A whole step is two frets
music_lessons_technique_bend_half_step_t: A half step bend aims for {note}, 1 fret up.
music_lessons_technique_bend_measure_tex: The microphone measures where the bend settles. It does so once you've held it steady for {settle} ms, or after {prompt} seconds if you never do. A bend counts as held after {hold} ms steady.
music_lessons_technique_bend_ring_text: Bend with the ring finger. When the fret leaves room, put the first and second fingers behind it on the same string, so all three push together. Turn the wrist and forearm to push the string across the neck, not only the fingertip.
music_lessons_technique_bend_start_step: Start on the fretted note, here {note} on string {string}.
music_lessons_technique_bend_target_text: The drill shows your string and fret, names the target note and draws it as a dashed line. To hear it first, fret the target on the same string, 1 fret up for a half step or 2 for a whole step. The app can't bend, so each button plays the two frets one after the other.
music_lessons_technique_bend_vibrato_tex: In the vibrato exercise you hold a guitar note and rock the string a little, evenly. A try counts when the drill hears vibrato, and it shows the rate, the width in cents and how even it was without scoring them. The app can't play vibrato either.

In the vibrato exercise you hold a ukulele note and rock the string a little, evenly. A try counts when the drill hears vibrato, and it shows the rate, the width in cents and how even it was without scoring them. The app can't play vibrato either.
music_lessons_technique_bend_whole_step_: A whole step bend aims for {note}, 2 frets up.
music_lessons_technique_landing_against_: Listen to the drone, think of the note an interval away, then finger it and play. The drill checks that the note your keys send is the target, not fine tuning. The bite can bend pitch without changing the note.
music_lessons_technique_landing_checks_t: Play the target and hold it for {seconds} seconds. The hold starts at your first target note, so a wrong fingering first costs nothing. It passes with the right pitch, the full hold and a steady breath, and an interval that would leave the chart's range asks you for another drone or direction.
music_lessons_technique_landing_hear_tex: Tap an interval and direction to hear the drone alone, then the landing note joining it. Notes are named as written, in your reading key, and the picture shows both notes.
music_lessons_technique_landing_land_tex: A drone sounds, and you land the note an interval above or below it: {intervals}. You set the interval, the direction and the drone.
music_lessons_technique_levels_hear_text: Each button plays a note at the middle of its band, louder for a higher level. The drill reads your breath, not the loudness of a note, and the app can't play a breath, so this is only a picture of soft to loud.
music_lessons_technique_levels_hold_text: A level asks you to hold at one loudness, from pp to f, by keeping the breath reading inside a band: {bands}. The {first} and {second} bands overlap a little.
music_lessons_technique_levels_scored_te: In Practice the breath trace shows a dashed line at the middle of the band. Half the score is the share of the hold with your breath inside the band, and the hold passes only when most of it is. These bands are starting values, so where soft and loud land depends on your sensor and how you blow.
music_lessons_technique_long_tone_breath: A long tone is a single note held for the whole time, with the air as even as you can keep it. The Aerophone's breath sensor tells the app how hard you blow, and the drill scores how still that stays.
music_lessons_technique_long_tone_checks: Tap the note on the chart, pick a hold of {seconds} seconds, and play. The hold starts at your first target note and passes with the right pitch, the full length and a steady breath, where drifting up or down counts against you as much as shaking. Without the breath sensor, only the pitch and the length are measured.
music_lessons_technique_long_tone_hear_t: Hear it plays a note at one fixed loudness for three seconds. The app can't play your breath, so this shows the pitch and the length, not how your air should feel. The breath sensor reads from 0 for no air to 1 for full (it arrives as MIDI CC 2).
music_lessons_technique_palm_counts_text: A note that is neither of the two is a stray, and the drill counts them. The chart's palm fingerings are best-effort until checked on your AE-20.
music_lessons_technique_palm_reach_text: The chart starts the palm keys at {note}, with the {first} key, and higher notes add {rest}. These crossings are {pairs}.
music_lessons_technique_palm_together_te: Where a fingering adds palm keys, press them at the same moment as the other keys change. A key that moves early or late sounds as a stray note between the two.
music_lessons_technique_pedal_after_text: The sustain pedal keeps notes ringing after you let go of the keys. Play the chord, then press the pedal, and the chord keeps sounding while your hands move. Tap Next to hear both.
music_lessons_technique_pedal_change_tex: At the next chord, play it, then lift the pedal just after it sounds and press straight back down. The old chord stops and the new one rings. Here that's {from} to {to}.
music_lessons_technique_pedal_change_tit: Up and down at the change
music_lessons_technique_pedal_checks_tex: After each new chord the pedal must lift within {lift} ms of the chord's first note and be down again within {repress} ms. A lift up to {early} ms before the chord still counts, and an earlier one is early. On the first chord the pedal only needs to be down within {repress} ms.
music_lessons_technique_pedal_clean_text: Lift {lift} ms after the chord and be down again {down} ms after it, and the change is clean. The drill reads a sustain pedal's CC 64 over MIDI, and counts the pedal as down from {downAt} percent. With no pedal arriving, nothing is measured.
music_lessons_technique_pedal_down_step: Press the pedal straight back down, so the new chord rings.
music_lessons_technique_pedal_lift_step: Play {chord}, then lift the pedal just after it sounds.
music_lessons_technique_pedal_no_pedal_s: Play {chord} and let go, with no pedal: it stops when your hands leave the keys.
music_lessons_technique_pedal_order_text: Lifting before the new chord leaves a gap, and holding the pedal through the change blurs the two chords together. The app can't press a pedal, so each button changes how long the first chord rings instead.
music_lessons_technique_pedal_with_pedal: Play {chord}, then press the pedal just after it sounds: it keeps ringing after you let go.
music_lessons_technique_pinky_counts_tex: A note that is neither of the two is a stray, and the drill counts them. Several of the chart's fingerings for these low notes are best-effort until checked on your instrument.
music_lessons_technique_pinky_slide_text: These crossings are {pairs}: a little finger changes from one pinky key to another. The chart shows which other keys change with it.
music_lessons_technique_pinky_together_t: Change the pinky key at the same moment as any other key that differs. A key that moves early or late sounds as a stray note between the two.
music_lessons_technique_register_break_t: A crossing goes back and forth between two notes whose fingerings differ, in eighths, with no stray note in between. On the chart, each note from {note} up to the top of the octave uses the fingering of the note an octave below, plus the +1 key under the left thumb.
music_lessons_technique_register_checks_: It scores the notes that are right, how even the spacing is, and the stray notes between the two. Names here are written notes, as on the chart.
music_lessons_technique_register_first_t: Many of the chart's fingerings are best-effort and not yet checked on a real AE-20. Where the chart disagrees with your instrument, trust the instrument.
music_lessons_technique_register_togethe: The common slip is a stray note between the two, because the keys didn't all change at the same moment. Step through this crossing's two fingerings and change only the keys that differ, all at once.
